source: Parsed from systemslibrarian/crypto-lab main: index.html cards, TITLE_TO_SECTION, LEARNING_PATHS, concept-coverage.md filing lines, and the five public course-module sequences.

exhibits.title: Quantum Vault KpqC
exhibits.copy: Threshold short-secret encryption using secret sharing and Korean post-quantum cryptography, compiled to WASM for direct browser use.

exhibits.title: Phantom Vault
exhibits.copy: Derive any password from a master passphrase using HMAC-DRBG. Nothing stored, nothing synced, nothing left behind to breach.

exhibits.title: Corrupted Oracle
exhibits.copy: A live Dual_EC_DRBG backdoor demo showing state recovery and future-output prediction while standard statistical tests still appear clean.

exhibits.title: Air Stream
exhibits.copy: Generate 128-EEA1, 128-EEA2 and 128-EEA3 keystream from one key, COUNT, bearer and direction, and check each against the test vectors in its own specification.

exhibits.title: KpqC Pair
exhibits.copy: Historical AIM2-based AIMer signing, with a reported public-key-only forgery vulnerability (ePrint 2026/2235, September 28, 2026), beside NTRU+ from the older NTRU line. Honest round trips do not establish signature security.

exhibits.title: TC26 Pair
exhibits.copy: Two TC26 post-quantum signature proposals side by side: code-based Shipovnik and stateless hash-based Hypericum, both built over Streebog.

exhibits.title: SM2 Forge
exhibits.copy: Sign and encrypt under GB/T 32918 SM2, read the identity digest that precedes every signature, compare both deployed ciphertext orders, then recover a key from a reused nonce.

exhibits.title: Misty Lens
exhibits.copy: Run MISTY1 and KASUMI side by side, map the design changes between them, and execute the seven-round related-key sandwich distinguisher in the page.

exhibits.title: Export Grade
exhibits.copy: Run real TETRA TEA1, trace its 80-bit key into a 32-bit working register, recover that register in a browser-sized window, then extrapolate the rate your own browser measured out to 2^80 and 2^128 and set it beside the published attacks on full-round AES.

exhibits.title: DRBG Arena
exhibits.copy: HMAC_DRBG, CTR_DRBG, and Hash_DRBG with state visualizers, seeding, reseeding, and live NIST SP 800-22 statistical tests. The correct-case companion to Corrupted Oracle.

exhibits.title: BB84
exhibits.copy: Quantum key distribution with photon polarization, basis sifting, QBER eavesdropper detection, and privacy amplification before AES-256-GCM message encryption.

exhibits.title: Shor
exhibits.copy: Modular period finding with QFT and continued fractions to recover integer factors, showing why RSA, ECC, and Diffie-Hellman must migrate to post-quantum alternatives.

exhibits.title: Grover
exhibits.copy: Amplitude amplification and oracle phase kickback for symmetric-key search, with live probability oscillation and concrete key-size impact (AES-128 to AES-256).

exhibits.title: Model Breach
exhibits.copy: A HiAE threat-model case study showing candidate enumeration, MITM state recovery, and guess-and-determine attacks when assumptions drift from deployment reality.

exhibits.title: Iron Letter
exhibits.copy: ECIES P-256 and RSA-OAEP compared side by side with live timing, key-size tradeoffs, and a simple sealed-letter mental model.

exhibits.title: Shadow Vault
exhibits.copy: One container, two passphrases, two messages. A practical demonstration of plausible deniability, forensic ambiguity, and browser-first UX around serious primitives.

exhibits.title: ZK Proof Lab
exhibits.copy: Six exhibits from Ali Baba cave to zk-SNARK intuition, with real Schnorr arithmetic, commitments, and replayable transcripts instead of vague metaphors.

exhibits.title: STARK Tower
exhibits.copy: AIR constraints, FRI polynomial commitments, and end-to-end Fibonacci proof. No trusted setup, post-quantum secure. The protocol behind StarkNet, StarkEx, and Risc Zero.

exhibits.title: SNARK Arena
exhibits.copy: Groth16 vs PLONK — trusted setup ceremonies, proof size comparison, the toxic waste problem, and production deployments in Zcash, Polygon zkEVM, WorldID, and zkLogin.

exhibits.title: Blind Oracle
exhibits.copy: A server adds encrypted values with TFHE-rs while the decryption key stays in your browser. See why a client must keep decryption-error feedback private.

exhibits.title: CKKS Lab
exhibits.copy: Approximate FHE for encrypted floating-point arithmetic, homomorphic neural network inference, rescaling, and the complete FHE trilogy (TFHE + BGV/BFV + CKKS).

exhibits.title: FHE Arena
exhibits.copy: BGV/BFV integer FHE — homomorphic addition and multiplication, live noise budget visualizer, relinearization, SIMD batching, and real-world deployments in private genomics and encrypted databases.

exhibits.title: Patron Shield
exhibits.copy: Information-theoretic private information retrieval applied to catalog privacy. A direct bridge from library ethics to concrete mathematical guarantees.

exhibits.title: VSS Gate
exhibits.copy: Feldman VSS and Pedersen VSS — verifiable secret sharing with live cheating dealer detection, commitment verification, and the layer beneath FROST and threshold wallets.

exhibits.title: DKG Gate
exhibits.copy: Pedersen/GJKR dealerless key generation — n parties Feldman-deal to each other, public complaints disqualify cheating dealers, and the sharings sum into one t-of-n key nobody ever held. Includes the rushing-adversary bias attack and its fix.

exhibits.title: Garbled Gate
exhibits.copy: Yao’s Garbled Circuits — gate-by-gate garbling, oblivious transfer for input wires, and the Millionaire’s Problem solved end-to-end. The foundational two-party MPC protocol.

exhibits.title: Silent Tally
exhibits.copy: Five hospitals compute a combined enrollment total without revealing any individual counts, demonstrating additive-homomorphic MPC in the browser.

exhibits.title: FROST Threshold
exhibits.copy: A browser-based FROST (RFC 9591) walkthrough where any qualified signer subset can produce one standard Ed25519 signature without key reassembly.

exhibits.title: Dilithium Seal
exhibits.copy: CRYSTALS-Dilithium (ML-DSA) digital signatures in the browser. Generate lattice-based key pairs, sign documents, and verify — all post-quantum safe.

exhibits.title: Ratchet Wire
exhibits.copy: A live walkthrough of the Double Ratchet protocol powering Signal-style messaging, with per-message key derivation and forward secrecy guarantees.

exhibits.title: Kyber Vault
exhibits.copy: CRYSTALS-Kyber (ML-KEM) key encapsulation in the browser. Encapsulate, decapsulate, and compare lattice-based key exchange against classical ECDH.

exhibits.title: Iron Serpent
exhibits.copy: The Serpent block cipher — AES finalist with a deeper security margin. Avalanche analysis, a security-margin (round-count) view, and side-by-side AES comparison.

exhibits.title: World Ciphers
exhibits.copy: Camellia (Japan), ARIA (South Korea), SM4 (China), and Kuznyechik (Russia) side by side with AES. Encrypt/decrypt playgrounds, S-box analysis, and geopolitical compliance context.

exhibits.title: Shamir Gate
exhibits.copy: Split a secret into shares using Shamir's Secret Sharing and reconstruct with any qualified threshold subset. Polynomial interpolation made tangible.

exhibits.title: Dead Sea Cipher
exhibits.copy: Substitution and polyalphabetic ciphers from Atbash to Vigenère, through to modern AES-256-GCM. Encode, decode, and explore classical cryptanalysis.

exhibits.title: SPHINCS+ Ledger
exhibits.copy: Stateless hash-based signatures (SLH-DSA) in the browser. A post-quantum signing scheme that relies only on the security of hash functions.

exhibits.title: Biham Lens
exhibits.copy: A live differential cryptanalysis attack on a toy SPN cipher — the technique co-invented by Biham and Shamir that broke reduced-round DES. DDT visualization and last-round key recovery.

exhibits.title: Hybrid Wire
exhibits.copy: X25519 + ML-KEM-768 hybrid post-quantum key exchange as deployed in Chrome 131+ and Cloudflare. Chrome 124 shipped the Kyber draft, not ML-KEM. Six-step handshake visualization and encrypted chat.

exhibits.title: Downgrade Wire
exhibits.copy: Strip X25519MLKEM768 from a TLS 1.3 ClientHello and watch two PQ-capable endpoints agree on classical X25519 — then turn on the Finished MAC and watch transcript binding abort the same strip.

exhibits.title: Babel Hash
exhibits.copy: SHA-256, SHA3-256, and BLAKE3 side by side with live avalanche visualization, length extension attack demo, and HMAC defense.

exhibits.title: AES Modes
exhibits.copy: ECB, CBC, CTR, GCM, and CCM with live padding oracle attack. Real WebCrypto operations, ECB penguin visualization, and authenticated encryption comparison.

exhibits.title: Educational RSA
exhibits.copy: Step-by-step RSA on real small numbers — key generation, encryption, decryption, and signatures — then watch a weak key get factored in milliseconds while a 2048-bit key holds. Real BigInt math, no backend.

exhibits.title: RSA Forge
exhibits.copy: Textbook RSA, OAEP, PSS signatures, and live attacks including small exponent and Bleichenbacher PKCS#1 v1.5 padding oracle. Real WebCrypto operations.

exhibits.title: Curve Lens
exhibits.copy: Point addition, scalar multiplication, and live ECDH across P-256, Curve25519, secp256k1, and brainpoolP256r1, whose RFC 5639 seeds it recomputes from π and e. P-256's seed has no published derivation.

exhibits.title: Point Arithmetic
exhibits.copy: Drag P and Q to see the chord-and-tangent group law, flip ℝ↔𝔽ₚ to run the identical exact arithmetic, then step double-and-add and feel why the ECDLP is hard.

exhibits.title: X3DH Wire
exhibits.copy: The asynchronous handshake behind Signal. Real X25519 arithmetic, four DH operations, and HKDF-SHA-256 key derivation — no backends, no simulated math.

exhibits.title: Noise Pipe
exhibits.copy: NN, XX, IK, and IKpsk2 handshake patterns with real X25519 arithmetic, live transport encryption, and a WireGuard deep dive.

exhibits.title: MAC Race
exhibits.copy: HMAC, CMAC, Poly1305, and GHASH compared with live length extension attack, timing attack, and nonce reuse demonstrations. Real WebCrypto operations.

exhibits.title: KDF Chain
exhibits.copy: HKDF, PBKDF2, scrypt, and Argon2id compared side by side with live parameter tuning, real timing measurements, and a KDF decision tree.

exhibits.title: Format Ward
exhibits.copy: FF1 and FF3-1 tokenization of credit cards, SSNs, and phone numbers — with the linear cryptanalysis that got FF3-1 cut from NIST's draft revision.

exhibits.title: Padding Oracle
exhibits.copy: Full Vaudenay 2002 chosen-ciphertext attack with real AES-CBC, byte-by-byte plaintext recovery, and coverage of ASP.NET, Lucky Thirteen, and POODLE.

exhibits.title: Timing Oracle
exhibits.copy: String comparison leakage, HMAC verification timing, RSA private key bit leakage, and cache-timing attacks with real performance.now() measurements.

exhibits.title: McEliece Gate
exhibits.copy: The oldest post-quantum KEM (1978). Binary Goppa codes, visceral 261KB public key visualization, and four-way comparison against ML-KEM, BIKE, and HQC.

exhibits.title: Frodo Vault
exhibits.copy: Conservative post-quantum KEM using plain LWE with no ring structure. LWE from first principles, error distribution, and side-by-side comparison against ML-KEM.

exhibits.title: BIKE Vault
exhibits.copy: Code-based post-quantum KEM using QC-MDPC codes, Black-Gray-Flip decoding, and side-by-side comparison against ML-KEM. NIST Round 4 alternate candidate.

exhibits.title: HQC Vault
exhibits.copy: Hamming Quasi-Cyclic post-quantum KEM with Reed-Muller/Reed-Solomon decoding, and three-way comparison against BIKE and ML-KEM.

exhibits.title: Falcon Seal
exhibits.copy: Compact NTRU lattice signatures with Fast Fourier Sampling, side-by-side comparison against ML-DSA and SLH-DSA, and implementation security warnings.

exhibits.title: ChaCha20 Stream
exhibits.copy: Quarter-round stepper, keystream visualizer, nonce reuse attack demo, and encrypt/decrypt playground. ARX design, no AES-NI required.

exhibits.title: Ed25519 Forge
exhibits.copy: Keypair generation, signing, and signature verification — deterministic nonces, tamper detection, the ZIP215 cofactor pitfall, and 64-byte compact signatures.

exhibits.title: Hash Zoo
exhibits.copy: SHA-256 vs SHA3-256 vs BLAKE3 internals — live avalanche analysis, Merkle-Damgård/sponge/tree construction diagrams, and timing benchmarks.

exhibits.title: World Hashes
exhibits.copy: SM3 (China), Streebog (Russia), and Kupyna (Ukraine) alongside SHA-256 and SHA-3. Five-way simultaneous hashing, avalanche analysis, and cryptographic sovereignty context.

exhibits.title: KDF Arena
exhibits.copy: Live timing and memory comparison of HKDF, PBKDF2, scrypt, and Argon2id with adjustable cost parameters and bar chart visualization.

exhibits.title: Poly1305 MAC
exhibits.copy: Polynomial evaluation over GF(2¹³⁰−5), constant-time tag verification, key-reuse attack visualizer, and Polynomial Stepper.

exhibits.title: OT Gate
exhibits.copy: 1-of-2 Oblivious Transfer using the Simplest OT protocol (Chou-Orlandi 2015) over Curve25519 with real Edwards25519 group arithmetic and AES-256-GCM encryption. Foundational primitive for secure MPC.

exhibits.title: LMS Ledger
exhibits.copy: LMS/HSS stateful hash-based signatures (NIST SP 800-208) — LM-OTS key state grid, one-time key reuse attack with real forgery demo, and CNSA 2.0 firmware signing context.

exhibits.title: Merkle Vault
exhibits.copy: The structural view: draw a tree up to 16 leaves with real SHA-256, walk one proof climb level by level, then mount a second-preimage attack and an append-only consistency check on the tree you built.

exhibits.title: Nonce Guard
exhibits.copy: AES-GCM vs AES-GCM-SIV comparison — live nonce reuse attack showing keystream XOR recovery and GHASH key extraction, synthetic IV construction, and misuse-resistance comparison. RFC 8452.

exhibits.title: Pairing Gate
exhibits.copy: BLS12-381 bilinear pairing — BLS signature sign/verify with real @noble/curves arithmetic, signature aggregation visualizer (up to 100 signers → 1 proof), and rogue key attack demo. Powers Ethereum 2.0 and Zcash.

exhibits.title: Oblivious Shelf
exhibits.copy: 2-server XOR Private Information Retrieval (Chor et al. 1995) — a patron retrieves any book from a 16-item catalog without the server learning which one was requested. Step-by-step query walkthrough and privacy audit.

exhibits.title: Stego Suite
exhibits.copy: LSB substitution, DCT-domain hiding, and adaptive embedding with live chi-squared steganalysis. Hide the message, not just the content.

exhibits.title: GG20 Wallet
exhibits.copy: GG20 threshold ECDSA — Paillier encryption, distributed key generation, and joint signing without any party holding the full private key. The protocol behind Fireblocks and Coinbase MPC.

exhibits.title: Bcrypt Forge
exhibits.copy: Bcrypt anatomy, cost factor benchmarking, timing-safe verification, and a real-world breach simulation. The workhorse password hash, dissected.

exhibits.title: Blind Sign
exhibits.copy: Chaum RSA blind signatures and Schnorr EC blind signatures — anonymous e-cash, private voting, and unlinkability proofs. The signer signs without seeing the message.

exhibits.title: Commit Gate
exhibits.copy: Hash commitments and Pedersen commitments — binding, hiding, sealed-bid auction, and homomorphic addition. The primitive beneath ZKPs, MPC, and VSS.

exhibits.title: PKI Chain
exhibits.copy: X.509 certificate chains, trust store validation, CA compromise cascades, Certificate Transparency with Merkle inclusion proofs, and post-quantum migration to ML-DSA.

exhibits.title: Protocol Compose
exhibits.copy: MAC-then-Encrypt vs Encrypt-then-MAC, padding oracle attack, CRIME, and the composition failures that drove TLS 1.3. Safe primitives composed unsafely break everything.

exhibits.title: Ring Sign
exhibits.copy: LSAG ring signatures — key image linkability, double-spend detection, group signatures with manager opening, and Monero transaction privacy. Sign as one-of-many without revealing which.

exhibits.title: Threshold Decrypt
exhibits.copy: ElGamal over P-256 — distributed key generation, verifiable partial decryptions with NIZK proofs, and t-of-n combination without any party holding the full private key.

exhibits.title: J-UNIWARD
exhibits.copy: JPEG steganography via Universal Wavelet Relative Distortion — adaptive DCT coefficient embedding that minimizes wavelet-domain detectability. The state-of-the-art in content-adaptive JPEG steganography.

exhibits.title: Harvest Vault
exhibits.copy: Why harvested traffic is already lost: capture a real key exchange, upgrade to post-quantum afterwards, and watch the recording stay just as readable. Mosca's theorem applied to what you already sent.

exhibits.title: Isogeny Gate
exhibits.copy: Elliptic-curve isogenies with a toy CSIDH over GF(419), supersingular graph walks, the Castryck-Decru break of SIDH, and the surviving branches of the field in SQIsign.

exhibits.title: Lattice Fault
exhibits.copy: Implementation attacks on lattice PQC: NTT power leakage, rejection-sampling fault bypass, KyberSlash timing, and a loop-abort fault that recovers a whole ML-DSA secret from one signature. The math survives; sloppy implementations do not.

exhibits.title: LLL Break
exhibits.copy: Step-by-step LLL and BKZ lattice reduction with Gram-Schmidt views, Lovasz condition checks, and a toy LWE primal attack that shows why Kyber-sized parameters do not fall the same way.

exhibits.title: MPCitH Sign
exhibits.copy: Post-quantum signatures from MPC-in-the-Head with additive secret sharing, SHA-256 commitments, Merkle proofs, Fiat-Shamir, and hidden-view challenges over a toy PERK-style witness.

exhibits.title: OPAQUE Gate
exhibits.copy: RFC 9807 OPAQUE aPAKE with live OPRF blind/evaluate/unblind flow, credential-envelope handling, 3DH mutual authentication, and server-breach simulation showing the password never reaches the server.

exhibits.title: VRF Gate
exhibits.copy: ECVRF prove/verify, Wesolowski VDF repeated squaring, and a RANDAO-plus-VDF beacon simulation that shows how verifiable randomness resists last-reveal manipulation.

exhibits.title: AEGIS Gate
exhibits.copy: AEGIS-256 as described in CFRG Informational RFC 10032, with AES round-function state updates, six-register sponge flow, tag derivation, and RFC test-vector verification in the browser.

exhibits.title: Ascon
exhibits.copy: NIST's lightweight cryptography standard with Ascon-AEAD128, Ascon-Hash256, avalanche analysis, and side-by-side comparison against AES-GCM and ChaCha20-Poly1305.

exhibits.title: Curve448
exhibits.copy: X448 key exchange and Ed448 signatures side by side with Curve25519 and Ed25519, covering the 224-bit security tier for long-lived keys.

exhibits.title: Dilithium Reject
exhibits.copy: An ML-DSA rejection-sampling lab with live acceptance histograms, rejection-reason breakdowns, and the signing-time tradeoff that keeps lattice signatures secure.

exhibits.title: ECDSA Forge
exhibits.copy: ECDSA on secp256k1 and P-256 with sign/verify workflows, RFC 6979 deterministic nonces, and the classic nonce-reuse private-key recovery attack.

exhibits.title: Schnorr Forge
exhibits.copy: Real BIP-340 Schnorr on secp256k1 with sign/verify, the step-by-step signing equation, nonce-reuse private-key recovery, and the linearity behind multisig and threshold signing.

exhibits.title: ElGamal Plain
exhibits.copy: Taher ElGamal's 1985 scheme with fresh ephemeral randomness, multiplicative homomorphism, and ciphertext rerandomization across toy and RFC 3526 groups.

exhibits.title: Harvest Timeline
exhibits.copy: The planning half of harvest-now-decrypt-later: which assets in a fleet cross a CRQC, what each year of delay costs, and what a migration actually reaches when you execute one.

exhibits.title: HAWK
exhibits.copy: An educational HAWK lab covering integer-only lattice signatures, discrete Gaussian sampling over Z, and the July 2026 key-recovery attack that led to HAWK's withdrawal from NIST's additional-signatures process.

exhibits.title: HQC Timing Break
exhibits.copy: A full-decryption oracle on HQC, where compiler rewrites reintroduce cache timing into constant-time source. Substitutes a repetition code for HQC's Reed-Muller inner code so the soft-decoding step stays legible.

exhibits.title: Hybrid Sign
exhibits.copy: Ed25519 plus ML-DSA-65 hybrid signatures per the IETF LAMPS composite-signature draft, framed as defense in depth for long-lived authenticity.

exhibits.title: IBE Gate
exhibits.copy: Boneh-Franklin identity-based encryption on BLS12-381 with setup, private-key extraction, encrypt/decrypt flow, and an honest look at the escrow tradeoff.

exhibits.title: KyberSlash
exhibits.copy: A KyberSlash timing-attack lab for ML-KEM, covering secret-dependent division, vulnerable compression paths, the Barrett-reduction fix, and live attack simulation.

exhibits.title: LMS/XMSS
exhibits.copy: State-managed hash-based signatures with LM-OTS, Merkle trees, and hierarchical composition, showing where LMS, HSS, and XMSS fit in practice.

exhibits.title: NTRU Classic
exhibits.copy: The original 1996 NTRU lattice cryptosystem with polynomial-ring arithmetic from scratch and the historical path from classic NTRU to modern post-quantum design.

exhibits.title: ORAM Vault
exhibits.copy: A Path ORAM walkthrough with tree buckets, stash growth, position-map updates, and adversary-view visualization for cloud access-pattern hiding.

exhibits.title: Paillier Gate
exhibits.copy: Paillier's additive homomorphic cryptosystem with encrypt/decrypt, tallying without decryption, and direct links to voting systems and GG20 threshold ECDSA.

exhibits.title: PQ Rotation
exhibits.copy: A post-quantum migration planner for hybrid certificates, multi-jurisdiction timelines, rolling key rotation, canary deployment, and rollback strategy.

exhibits.title: PQ TLS Handshake
exhibits.copy: TLS 1.3 with the X25519MLKEM768 hybrid handshake, including byte-level framing, full key schedule derivation, and comparison against classical X25519.

exhibits.title: PSI Gate
exhibits.copy: Classic DH-PSI over ristretto255 with RFC 9380 hash-to-curve, showing how two parties learn their overlap (and each other's set size) and nothing more.

exhibits.title: Scloud+ Vault
exhibits.copy: China's conservative LWE-based KEM with ternary secrets, BW32 lattice coding, and a faithful but simplified browser model of the ePrint 2024/1306 design.

exhibits.title: Threshold ML-DSA
exhibits.copy: A two-party demo of distributed post-quantum signing that produces real FIPS 204 ML-DSA signatures; key-non-reconstruction is illustrated, not enforced.

exhibits.title: Envelope KMS
exhibits.copy: RFC 3394/5649 AES key wrap, DEK/KEK hierarchy, KMS-style key rotation, re-wrap without plaintext exposure, and a hash-chained audit log — the architecture behind AWS KMS and Google Cloud KMS.

exhibits.title: Bulletproofs
exhibits.copy: ZK range proofs using Bulletproofs on ristretto255 — 64-bit Pedersen commitments, aggregate proofs over multiple ranges, the inner-product argument, and a tamper-rejection demo.

exhibits.title: Nonce Lattice
exhibits.copy: ECDSA nonce-bias lattice attack on secp256k1 and P-256 — Hidden Number Problem construction, in-browser LLL reduction, and byte-for-byte private-key recovery from biased nonces.

exhibits.title: Kerberos v5
exhibits.copy: RFC 4120 Kerberos v5 — Needham-Schroeder origins, Lowe attack, full AS/TGS/AP exchange flow, AES-256-CTS-HMAC-SHA1-96 ticket encryption, and clock-skew replay defense.

exhibits.title: MLS Group
exhibits.copy: RFC 9420 Messaging Layer Security — TreeKEM ratchet tree, epoch key schedule, member add/remove/update operations, and group application messaging with forward secrecy guarantees.

exhibits.title: ZK Arena
exhibits.copy: A side-by-side comparison playground for zk-SNARK and zk-STARK proof systems — setup phases, proving overhead, verification cost, and the tradeoff space between Groth16, PLONK, and STARKs.

exhibits.title: Jevil
exhibits.copy: A hash-based few-time signature scheme over the Goldilocks field using Lagrange interpolation — bounded-use signing with reusable verification keys.

exhibits.title: Ciphertext Mirror
exhibits.copy: An ML-KEM side-channel walkthrough — manipulating ciphertexts through the Fujisaki-Okamoto transform, LDPC decoder behavior, and NTT blinding countermeasures.

exhibits.title: HQC Timing
exhibits.copy: The 2020 timing attack on HQC's BCH decoder — the parameterization predating today's Reed-Muller/Reed-Solomon — reproduced with a modelled decode time rather than a real decoder, then silenced by constant-time.

exhibits.title: PQ Families
exhibits.copy: A guided tour of the five post-quantum problem families — lattice, code-based, hash-based, multivariate, and isogeny — with the assumptions, history, and standardization status of each.

exhibits.title: Key Exchange
exhibits.copy: A walkthrough of key exchange across history and protocol families — from Diffie-Hellman to modern hybrid post-quantum handshakes, with shared assumptions and threat models per era.

exhibits.title: Web of Trust
exhibits.copy: A PGP-style trust graph — sign each other's keys, walk introduction chains, observe how trust flows (and breaks) without a central authority.

exhibits.title: WebAuthn
exhibits.copy: Passwordless authentication via FIDO2 / WebAuthn — assertion verification, origin binding, signature counters, and the journey from passwords to passkeys.

exhibits.title: SSH Handshake
exhibits.copy: SSH transport-layer handshake and TOFU host-key pinning — ephemeral X25519 / ECDH, Ed25519 signatures over the exchange hash, and known_hosts change detection across StrictHostKeyChecking modes.

exhibits.title: Bitcoin Wallet
exhibits.copy: Bitcoin wallet pipeline in the browser — secp256k1 keys to P2PKH and P2WPKH addresses via HASH160, plus BIP-39 mnemonics, PBKDF2 seed stretching, and BIP-32 hardened child derivation.

exhibits.title: Enigma Forge
exhibits.copy: Full mechanical Enigma — rotors with double-stepping, plugboard, and reflector — plus the crib-based Bombe break that exploits the flaw that no letter ever maps to itself.

exhibits.title: Vigenère Break
exhibits.copy: Encrypt and decrypt with a repeating-key Vigenère cipher, then recover the key length with Kasiski examination and the index of coincidence and solve each column by frequency analysis.

exhibits.title: OTP Vault
exhibits.copy: One-time pad encryption with provable perfect secrecy, then the two-time-pad break: XOR two ciphertexts under a reused key and crib-drag to recover both plaintexts.

exhibits.title: Collision Vault
exhibits.copy: Verify real published MD5 and SHA-1 collision pairs — SHAttered, identical-prefix, chosen-prefix — live in the browser, then watch SHA-256 and SHA-3 resist the same attack.

exhibits.title: JWT Forge
exhibits.copy: Paste or generate a JWT, tamper with claims, and swap algorithms to watch alg:none and HS/RS key-confusion attacks succeed against a vulnerable verifier and fail against a correct one.

exhibits.title: E91
exhibits.copy: Ekert's entanglement-based QKD: measure entangled pairs, run the CHSH Bell test, and derive a key from aligned bases. |S|≈2.83 proves security; an eavesdropper drags it toward the classical bound, so the key is discarded.

exhibits.title: Hybrid Guide
exhibits.copy: A guide to hybrid post-quantum key exchange — a KEM combiner pairs X25519 with ML-KEM-768 so the session key holds as long as either half survives. Break each component to see the hedge.

exhibits.title: Multivariate UOV
exhibits.copy: A real Unbalanced Oil-and-Vinegar scheme over GF(256) signs and verifies in the browser, showing how fixing the vinegar variables turns the MQ trapdoor into a linear solve — plus the 2022 Beullens attack that broke Rainbow.

exhibits.title: MAYO Seal
exhibits.copy: Runs real MAYO keygen, signing, and verification over GF(16), stepping through the moment an oil space too small to invert becomes solvable once k copies of the map are whipped together.

exhibits.title: LWE Hints
exhibits.copy: Counts how many leakage hints collapse an LWE lattice problem on sparse ternary secrets, then recovers a toy secret from real hints and tests the Gaussian assumption against sampled data. ePrint 2026/1081.

exhibits.title: Syndrome Drain
exhibits.copy: How code-based KEMs erode below NIST Level 1 when one public key derives many session keys — run a toy decode-one-of-many search and watch the measured work fall as √D, then compute when to rotate keys.

exhibits.title: Broken Trust
exhibits.copy: Leak one bit of ML-DSA's per-signature masking randomness and the secret subkey becomes the bottom of a hill you can roll down — no lattice reduction. Watch a toy version descend beside real-scale numbers from ePrint 2026/472.

exhibits.title: Bitcoin Script
exhibits.copy: Step a real P2PKH spend through the Script stack machine — valid, wrong-key, forged-signature, and tampered scenarios, with real secp256k1 and HASH160. No backend.

exhibits.title: DH MITM
exhibits.copy: Interactive Diffie-Hellman key exchange, then a live man-in-the-middle attack on the unauthenticated channel that shows why raw DH needs authentication. Real modular arithmetic. No backend.

exhibits.title: Hybrid PQC
exhibits.copy: Compare classical, post-quantum, and hybrid key exchange and signatures side by side, then break one half and watch the hybrid survive. Real X25519, ML-KEM-768, Ed25519, ML-DSA-65. No backend.

exhibits.title: Merkle Proofs
exhibits.copy: The proof-semantics view: what an inclusion proof does and does not establish — RFC 9162 index verification, a pinned real Certificate Transparency entry, and the RFC 6962 and CVE-2012-2459 attacks.

exhibits.title: PAKE Gate
exhibits.copy: Tour SRP-6a, J-PAKE, CPace, and Dragonfly (RFC 7664) side by side — a shared key forms from a low-entropy password that never crosses the wire, plus a server-breach toggle and the Dragonblood side-channel.

exhibits.title: Shamir vs FROST
exhibits.copy: Compare Shamir secret sharing against FROST signatures side by side — watch Shamir reassemble the key in memory while FROST signs without it ever existing. Real GF(256) and Ed25519. No backend.

exhibits.title: Time-Lock Puzzle
exhibits.copy: Seal a message that only sequential squaring can open, then reveal the creator's instant trapdoor that collapses the delay. Real BigInt and AES-256-GCM. No backend.

exhibits.title: Timing Side-Channel
exhibits.copy: Recover a hidden secret one byte at a time from an early-exit comparison, then watch a constant-time compare flatten the leak. Real performance.now() measurements. No backend.

exhibits.title: TLS Handshake
exhibits.copy: Step through X25519 key exchange, Ed25519 authentication, the HKDF key schedule, and AES-GCM records, with a MITM attack that gets blocked. Real WebCrypto. No backend.

exhibits.title: VDF
exhibits.copy: Repeated modular squaring in an RSA group with a Wesolowski short proof — watch sequential work accrue one squaring at a time, confirm parallel workers don't help, then verify instantly and reveal the trapdoor.

exhibits.title: Chain of Trust
exhibits.copy: X.509 path building vs RFC 5280 validation on a real cross-signed ECDSA hierarchy — build chains yourself, watch a naive builder fail a valid leaf, and see valid signatures rejected.

exhibits.title: KEM Trap
exhibits.copy: Real ML-KEM-768 decapsulation never fails loudly — flip a ciphertext bit and watch a caller that drops the return code or skips key confirmation turn implicit rejection into an oracle.

exhibits.title: Time Trust
exhibits.copy: Real Ed25519, HMAC, and X.509 verification driven by one movable clock — drag NOW and watch certificates, JWTs, TOTP codes, and replay caches change their verdicts about bytes that never change.

exhibits.title: Nonce Collision
exhibits.copy: Reuse one nonce under one key across AES-CTR, AES-GCM, ChaCha20-Poly1305, and AES-CBC — crib-drag plaintext out of XOR'd ciphertexts and forge tags the real verifiers accept.

exhibits.title: Signed Bytes
exhibits.copy: Real Ed25519 over JSON — a signature binds an exact byte string, never the parsed meaning. Break key order, Unicode, and duplicate keys, then watch JCS canonicalization fix some and refuse others.

exhibits.title: HPKE Envelope
exhibits.copy: RFC 9180 with every stage exposed — a KEM, a KDF, and an AEAD composed into one scheme; edit the info string or AAD and watch the real AEAD reject.

exhibits.title: Blind Hello
exhibits.copy: TLS 1.3 encrypts everything except the hostname it announces first — seal the ClientHello with real HPKE and see exactly what ECH hides, what it can't, and why it needs encrypted DNS.

exhibits.title: Blind Relay
exhibits.copy: Oblivious HTTP splits knowledge between a relay that sees your address and a gateway that sees your request — flip the collusion toggle and watch the guarantee evaporate.

exhibits.title: Key Mirror
exhibits.copy: A key directory that lies to one user and tells the truth to another — then the append-only Merkle log, consistency proofs, and gossip that make the lie detectable.

exhibits.title: SPAKE Gate
exhibits.copy: SPAKE2 and SPAKE2+ on the same password, side by side — indistinguishable until the server database leaks, then one impersonation costs nothing and the other forces an offline crack.

exhibits.title: Reshare Circle
exhibits.copy: Refresh threshold shares into a new epoch: every old share becomes garbage, the public key never changes, and the secret is never reconstructed along the way.

exhibits.title: Entropy Collapse
exhibits.copy: Restore two copies of a VM snapshot and watch an honest, standards-conformant HMAC_DRBG emit identical session keys from both — the seed, not the generator, is the whole game.

exhibits.title: Salamander
exhibits.copy: Build one AES-GCM ciphertext that decrypts to two different valid plaintexts under two different keys — both tags verify, because AEAD never promised they couldn't.

exhibits.title: Frozen Heart
exhibits.copy: Forge a Schnorr zero-knowledge proof the real verifier accepts — because the Fiat-Shamir challenge hash left one transcript field out of its input.

exhibits.title: Credential Veil
exhibits.copy: BBS+ selective disclosure over BLS12-381 — the issuer signs six fields once; the holder reveals any subset, unlinkably every time, and proves over-18 without a birth date.

exhibits.title: Power Trace
exhibits.copy: Recover an AES-128 key byte from power consumption alone. The cipher is correct and constant-time, yet CPA and DPA walk the key out through the power rail. Simulated traces, real statistics.

exhibits.title: Protocol Checker
exhibits.copy: A Dolev-Yao symbolic model checker that rediscovers Lowe's attack on Needham-Schroeder live — found by searching, not by being told — then closes the seventeen-year-old flaw in one edit.

exhibits.title: Quantum Entropy
exhibits.copy: A biased beam-splitter QRNG, Shannon vs min-entropy on the same stream, von Neumann debiasing, and a real Toeplitz extractor with Leftover Hash Lemma accounting and NIST SP 800-90B health tests.

exhibits.title: SPDZ Forge
exhibits.copy: SPDZ over F_p (2^61−1) — additive shares, Beaver triples, and information-theoretic MACs. Tamper with a share and semi-honest MPC swallows the lie while SPDZ aborts, even with a dishonest majority.

exhibits.title: Traitor Trace
exhibits.copy: Naor-Naor-Lotspiech subset-cover over a 16-leaf tree — one ciphertext for all subscribers, revoke a member without rekeying anyone, and trace a leaked decoder back to its builder. Real AES-256-GCM.

exhibits.title: Isogeny Atlas
exhibits.copy: A real supersingular isogeny graph over GF(431²), computed live from the modular polynomials, with the seven open problems of isogeny crypto drawn as paths, cycles, and endomorphisms.

exhibits.title: Syndrome Hints
exhibits.copy: A real information-set-decoding attack on syndrome decoding over F₂ — feed it leaked side-channel hints and watch the work factor slide from exponential toward polynomial.

exhibits.title: Lattice Gentle
exhibits.copy: The lattice picture underneath ML-KEM and ML-DSA: drag basis vectors through SVP and CVP, step Gauss and LLL, then run toy Kyber and Dilithium end to end.

exhibits.title: Encrochat
exhibits.copy: A real Double Ratchet exchange with a genuinely opaque wire, then a modelled endpoint implant reads the plaintext anyway. The cryptography held; it did not matter.

exhibits.title: Icy DVRF
exhibits.copy: A t-of-n distributed VRF: partial evaluations proven with Chaum-Pedersen DLEQ under one shared challenge, aggregating to a constant-size 128-byte proof whether three parties contribute or three hundred.

exhibits.title: MuSig Gate
exhibits.copy: n signers aggregate their public keys into one key and their nonces into one nonce, yielding a single Schnorr signature indistinguishable from a lone signer's — plus three live forgeries BIP-327 defeats.

exhibits.title: Ablation Wire
exhibits.copy: The 1942 Navajo code-talker stack rebuilt on modern primitives, with every layer independently switchable — turn one off and discover which was actually load-bearing.

exhibits.title: Accumulator
exhibits.copy: One fixed-size digest commits to a growing set. Prove a certificate is in it — or, the hard part, that it is not — with a short witness, then forge one with the trapdoor.

exhibits.title: Beacon Lock
exhibits.copy: Lock a ciphertext to a future drand round and let the beacon's BLS signature be the decryption key — identity-based encryption with a clock in place of an authority.

exhibits.title: Card Trick
exhibits.copy: den Boer's five-card trick — two players compute the AND of their secret bits from a shuffle alone, with security no amount of computing power can buy through.

exhibits.title: DP Noise
exhibits.copy: Real Laplace and Gaussian mechanisms over a twelve-person payroll — watch two databases differing by one person become indistinguishable, then watch averaging take the truth back once the budget is spent.

exhibits.title: Matsui Line
exhibits.copy: Matsui's Algorithm 2 against the same toy SPN Biham Lens attacks — count the bias in real known-plaintext traffic, watch one subkey candidate separate, then watch the piling-up lemma's prediction miss.

exhibits.title: Search Vault
exhibits.copy: An encrypted inverted index the server searches without a key — then the count and IKK leakage-abuse attacks turn the access pattern it observed back into your queries.

exhibits.title: Simon's Period
exhibits.copy: Exact statevector Simon's algorithm recovering a hidden XOR period in O(n) queries, then using it to predict an Even-Mansour ciphertext and forge a CBC-MAC tag.

exhibits.title: Stream Ward
exhibits.copy: Splitting a large file into individually authenticated segments fixes the memory ceiling and breaks ordering — reorder, drop or truncate the frames and every tag still verifies until a chain state binds them.

exhibits.title: KMAC Gate
exhibits.copy: SHA3-256, SHAKE, cSHAKE and KMAC driven by one hand-rolled Keccak-f[1600] permutation — step the sponge block by block, then tamper with a signed message and watch the real verifier reject it.

exhibits.title: Token Tell
exhibits.copy: Runs the real SynthID-Text keyed detector over watermarked text, then signs the same words with ECDSA P-256: change only the key and the statistical evidence vanishes; change one byte and verification fails outright.

exhibits.title: Context Ward
exhibits.copy: Seals an agent's context window into a SHA-256 hash chain with role-separated HMAC seals and Ed25519 tool attestations, then shows injected content passing every check while the agent is compromised anyway.

exhibits.title: Regex Veil — FTE
exhibits.copy: Compiles a regex to a minimal DFA, counts its length-n language exactly, and enciphers real AES-CTR bytes into that slice with FF1 — output a DPI rule accepts, plus the substitution attack proving nothing is authenticated.

exhibits.title: Shelf Oracle
exhibits.copy: Classic PIR needs two servers that never collude. This needs one, under RLWE. Watch the noise budget fall as the server folds in every record — it cannot see which one you asked for.

exhibits.title: Feistel Forge
exhibits.copy: Real DES stepped round by round, where the round function need not be invertible — and DES's is not. Then double DES falls to meet-in-the-middle, and a 64-bit block collides at the birthday bound.

exhibits.title: Rekey Relay
exhibits.copy: A semi-trusted relay turns Alice's ciphertext into Bob's without ever holding the plaintext. In BBS98, the scheme everyone starts with, the relay and Bob recover Alice's private key in one modular division.

exhibits.title: Polynomial Forge
exhibits.copy: One polynomial committed three ways — KZG, IPA, FRI — then the failure nothing else teaches: omit the degree bound and every cryptographic check still passes while the low-degree claim is gone.

exhibits.title: DNSSEC Chain
exhibits.copy: The PKI that has to sign statements about names which do not exist. Validate a real captured chain from the IANA anchor, then walk an NSEC3 zone the denial proofs gave away.

exhibits.title: Masked Core
exhibits.copy: First-order Boolean masking flattens the CPA that Power Trace runs — so combine two samples instead of one and the key byte comes back. Masking is a price, not a wall, and this measures it.

exhibits.title: Sector Vault
exhibits.copy: XTS-AES is what full-disk encryption actually uses. Flip a bit, copy a block, restore yesterday's sector — every read returns plaintext and raises nothing, because the mode has nothing to raise it with.

exhibits.title: Attribute Gate
exhibits.copy: Encrypt to a policy instead of to a person. Then splice two real keys whose attributes only jointly satisfy that policy, run the genuine decryption, and watch the term that refuses to cancel.

exhibits.title: Sphinx Mix
exhibits.copy: Peel a real Sphinx packet across three mixes — per-hop blinding, a header that never changes length. Then trace one sender end to end on a quiet network with every cryptographic check green.

exhibits.title: Attestation Gate
exhibits.copy: Measured boot into PCRs, a real TPMS_ATTEST quote, a verifier with reference values — then run something outside the measured set after the last measurement and watch every check pass.

exhibits.title: GGH Trapdoor
exhibits.copy: A lattice trapdoor is just a good basis: one lattice, two bases, and only the short one decrypts. Then two attacks read the secret off the shape of GGH's own randomness.

exhibits.title: Factor Forge
exhibits.copy: Seven classical factoring methods on a real BigInt N, each waiting for a different mistake in key generation. Obey every RSA rule and rho and ECM still finish; only size stops them.

exhibits.title: Privacy Pass
exhibits.copy: A token proves the issuer authorised someone without anyone — issuer, origin, or the two colluding — learning who. Remove the client's blind and nothing on the wire changes; the guarantee is simply gone.

exhibits.title: Order Leak
exhibits.copy: A column you can still sort or match on has already published the shape of its answers. Equality, order and a public distribution hand back the plaintext cell by cell — the key is never touched.

exhibits.title: Split Point
exhibits.copy: Secret-share a function, not a value: two DPF keys each evaluate to shares of one-at-α, zero everywhere else. Two non-colluding servers fold 65,536 records and neither learns which one you read.

exhibits.title: Proof Tally
exhibits.copy: Secret sharing hides a measurement and will happily add a lie to the total. A fully linear proof carried in the same shares lets two aggregators reject a malformed report neither of them can read.

exhibits.title: Fold Gate
exhibits.copy: Combining two satisfying R1CS instances leaves a computable cross term; relax the system with a slack scalar and an error vector to absorb it, and one folded instance stands in for all of them.

exhibits.title: Hidden Bit
exhibits.copy: Run the game: a challenger hides one bit, an adversary guesses. A rising advantage proves a scheme broken; a flat one proves only that these adversaries failed — which is why security needs a reduction.

exhibits.title: PQXDH Wire
exhibits.copy: One ML-KEM secret added to the X3DH transcript is what survives a future curve break. The prekey signature and the ratchet after it are untouched, so Bob can still be impersonated with every check green.

exhibits.title: Sleeve Check
exhibits.copy: GOST published a 256-byte S-box as a bare table. It falls out of four small constants and field arithmetic — evidence about how it was designed, which is not by itself an attack.

exhibits.title: Ghost Commit
exhibits.copy: Commit an API key, delete it two commits later, and it keeps its name and its contents forever — git adds objects, it never edits them. Then an entropy scanner finds it in seconds.

exhibits.title: Lattice Builder
exhibits.copy: Two dials straighten a scrambled lattice until its shortest vector is readable by eye. Then guess seven of a real Module-LWE key's eight coefficients and the error left over is no smaller than guessing none.

exhibits.title: Covert Channel Studio
exhibits.copy: The same bits moved eleven ways — DNS labels, ICMP echoes, inter-arrival gaps, packet order, cache lines — each scored by a cited detector. Then a warden closes several channels while their anomaly score falls, leaving no record.

exhibits.title: Point Ledger
exhibits.copy: Quantum resource estimates for secp256k1, a classical multiplication dialog, and where fuzz-test evidence stops supporting a Fiat-Shamir soundness claim.

exhibits.title: MGM Mode
exhibits.copy: MGM, the GOST AEAD mode (RFC 9058), over Magma and Kuznyechik: a distinct authentication coefficient per block against GCM's single H, every RFC test value checked, nonce reuse, and why 64-bit blocks re-key sooner.

exhibits.title: Drift Key
exhibits.copy: Turn a noisy reading that never repeats into the same key every time: a code-offset secure sketch over hand-built BCH codes, HKDF-SHA-256, and the exact entropy the public helper data costs.

exhibits.title: Noise to Numbers
exhibits.copy: NIST SP 800-90B min-entropy from pinned runs of the real assessment tool: a modelled Infinite Noise TRNG scores 0.37 bits per bit, a SHA-256 counter scores 0.92. Entropy belongs to the source, not the bytes.

exhibits.title: Pulse Chain
exhibits.copy: Recompute real NIST Beacon 2.0 pulses byte by byte, walk their SHA-512 hash chain and skiplist, verify drand rounds with a BLS12-381 pairing, and see what no check proves: whether the operator knew first.

exhibits.title: Glass Box
exhibits.copy: Chow-style white-box AES-128 built from your key as 2,032 encoded lookup tables, then attacked twice: differential computation analysis pulls the key from execution traces, and BGE step A1 strips the table encodings.

exhibits.title: Return Path
exhibits.copy: Impossible differentials and the boomerang attack on the same toy SPN as Biham Lens, with DDT and BCT tables computed live, an adaptive chosen-ciphertext oracle, and a one-way-impossible crossing every round trip closes.

exhibits.title: SM9 Forge
exhibits.copy: Extract an identity key by inverting in the exponent rather than hashing to a curve, run SM9’s signature, key exchange and encryption against the standard’s own worked examples, and see why two implementations agreeing doesn’t prove either followed the spec.

exhibits.title: PQ Chooser
exhibits.copy: Set what constrains you and get a shortlist of two or three post-quantum schemes to investigate, built from sizes it derives by running the real algorithms in your browser rather than quoting a table.

exhibits.title: Adaptor Gate
exhibits.copy: One click turns a pre-signature the real BIP-340 verifier rejects into a valid signature, then subtracts the two to read the secret back out — the fact that atomic swaps and PTLC routing are both built on.

exhibits.title: Function Key
exhibits.copy: Issue a key that answers one question about an encrypted vector — its weighted sum — and nothing else. Then issue keys one at a time and watch the set of possible plaintexts shrink, until one more key hands over the master secret.

exhibits.title: Locks and Keys
exhibits.copy: A padlock anyone may close and only you can open — real RSA-OAEP and RSA-PSS on a 2048-bit pair, with the wrong key failing on purpose and the same pair doing its other job, signing. No maths on screen.

exhibits.title: What Is PQC
exhibits.copy: Runs a real ML-KEM-768 exchange beside a real X25519 one in matching panels, so the only measurable difference is size — 2,272 bytes on the wire instead of 64. Not stronger: a different hard problem.

exhibits.title: HTTPS Padlock
exhibits.copy: Takes apart a certificate a real site presented, lets you break each of its four checks in turn, then shows a flawless certificate for a lookalike domain that passes every one. Reads captured certificates; it never connects to a site.

exhibits.title: Good Randomness
exhibits.copy: Two 32-byte keys pass the same look-random checks — one from the browser’s generator, one from a ChaCha20 stream started at a four-digit PIN. Then the second is rebuilt by counting to ten thousand, while every check still reports success.

exhibits.title: Agreeing in Public
exhibits.copy: The paint-mixing picture, then one real X25519 exchange with both sides’ secrets compared byte for byte — and a stranger who answers in Bob’s place while every check on the page still passes. No modulus, no exponent.

exhibits.title: Vector Gate
exhibits.kicker: A Verifier That Accepts a Forgery
exhibits.copy: Switch off Ed25519's required scalar-range check and watch the verifier accept a signature nobody signed, while all five RFC vectors still pass — then ask what passing them proved.

concepts.title: Delay, sequential work, and release conditions
Formal security analysis: symbolic and computational

paths.label: Start Here
paths.focus: No cryptography assumed. Beginner labs, in order.
paths.blurb: For a first visit, with no cryptography assumed: ciphers you can do on paper, then the fingerprint, where keys come from, public and private keys, agreeing on a secret in the open, the signature, the padlock, the password and the quantum clock. Thirteen steps, every one a Beginner lab -- no maths beyond arithmetic. One more is planned, on who can read your messages, and will be added when that lab lands.

sideTrip.title: Stego Suite
sideTrip.why: a different goal entirely — hiding that a message was sent at all. Sits beside the classical ciphers; take it or skip it.

paths.label: Developer Path
paths.focus: Primitives through to the protocols you actually ship.
paths.blurb: A builder's journey — from primitives to the protocols you actually ship.

paths.label: Cryptanalyst Path
paths.focus: Each class of attack in turn, classical ciphers to post-quantum.
paths.blurb: Mathematical attacks exploit structure and statistics; oracles exploit response differences; side channels measure timing or power; faults alter computation. Follow each from classical ciphers to PQC.

paths.label: Post-Quantum Path
paths.focus: PQ KEMs, signatures, hybrids and the migration itself.
paths.blurb: A focused track on PQ KEMs, signatures, hybrids, and migration.

paths.label: Key Exchange Path
paths.focus: How two parties agree on a secret, ECDH to hybrid handshakes.
paths.blurb: How two parties agree on a secret — classical ECDH to hybrid post-quantum handshakes.
